objectives: Name the modes of transport and compare their advantages
Describe the main transport links of Cameroon
Explain problems of transport and possible solutions

blocks.md: **Transport** is the movement of people and goods from one place to another. It links farms to markets, factories to ports and people to services. The main modes are **road**, **rail**, **water** (sea, river, lake) and **air**, plus pipelines for oil and gas. Good transport lowers costs and helps trade and national unity.

blocks.caption: Modes compared
blocks.alt: Four columns summarising road, rail, water and air transport.

blocks.title: Comparing modes
blocks.md:
- **Road**: flexible, door to door, good for short and medium distances; accidents and bad roads are problems.
- **Rail**: cheap for heavy goods over long distances; fixed routes.
- **Water**: very cheap for bulky goods; slow; needs ports.
- **Air**: fastest, for people and valuable or perishable goods; very expensive.

**Transport in Cameroon.** Roads carry most passengers and goods; main roads link Douala, Yaoundé, Bafoussam, Bamenda and the north, while many rural roads become muddy in the rainy season. The **railway** runs from Douala to Yaoundé and on to Ngaoundéré, carrying passengers and goods such as fuel, timber and cattle. **Douala** is the main seaport, serving also landlocked neighbours such as Chad and the Central African Republic. There are international airports at **Douala** and **Yaoundé**, plus others in regional centres.

blocks.title: Problems and solutions
blocks.md: **Problems**: poor and unpaved roads, potholes and floods, road accidents, congestion in cities, high fuel and fares, old vehicles. **Solutions**: building and maintaining roads and bridges, enforcing traffic rules, public transport (buses), developing railways and river transport, improving ports and airports, and local councils maintaining feeder roads. Better roads lower the price of food in towns and raise farmers' income.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- 'Best' mode depends on goods, distance and cost: no mode is always best.
- Landlocked countries depend on ports of neighbours; Cameroon is not landlocked.
- Do not mix up transport (movement) with communication (messages by phone and radio).

blocks.title: Example 1: choose a mode
blocks.statement: A company must send 500 tonnes of timber from Douala port to Europe. Which mode is best, and why?
steps: The goods are bulky and heavy and distance is great.
Water transport is cheapest for bulky goods over long distances.
blocks.answer: Sea transport, because it is cheapest for bulky cargo.

blocks.title: Example 2: perishable goods
blocks.statement: Fresh flowers must reach another continent within one day. Which mode is used and why?
steps: The goods spoil quickly, so speed matters more than cost.
blocks.answer: Air transport, because it is fastest.
